::: {#def-positional-invariance .theorem}
## Positional invariance

A component function $g_{ti}$ is positionally invariant with respect to network graph $\mathcal{G}_t=(\mathcal{N},\psi_t)$ if it (a) depends only on the neighbor values $\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i}$, and (b) is unchanged by a permutation of those values together with the same permutation of the network weights: for all $\mathbf{X},\mathbf{X}'\in\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{X}_t)$, all units $i,j$ and every permutation matrix $M$,

$$
\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i}=M\mathbf{X}'_{\mathcal{N}_j},\quad \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{i,\mathcal{N}_i}=M\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{j,\mathcal{N}_j}\ \Rightarrow\ g_{ti}(\mathbf{X})=g_{tj}(\mathbf{X}'),
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{i,\mathcal{N}_i}$ is $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_i$ restricted to the neighborhood of $i$. Equivalently, there is a single function $\gamma_t$ of finite multisets of (value, weight) pairs such that, for every unit $i$,

$$
g_{ti}(\mathbf{X})=\gamma_t\big(\{\!\!\{(X_j,\psi_t(i,j)):j\in\mathcal{N}_i\}\!\!\}\big).
$$

An exposure mapping is positionally invariant with respect to a graph set $\mathcal{H}=\{\mathcal{G}_t\}_{t\in\{1,\dots,T\}}$ if it is separable and each component function is positionally invariant with respect to an element of $\mathcal{H}$.
:::
